title: ₹3,000 Ka Hotel Room: 20 Rooms Wale Hotel Ka Owner Kitna Kamata Hai?
description: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. Hotels are on our list of dream-to-own businesses, and the breakeven-by-occupancy format matches reels that held attention, like the turf and gym ones. OTA commissions and RevPAR benchmarks are published, so the math can be shown on screen.
text:
**HISAAB FACT SHEET: 20-room budget or business hotel in India**
Research date: 3 Nov 2026. All figures come from web sources, and many are third-party or illustrative. Where sources conflict, I say so.

**⚠️ Angle check before you script**
- None of my sources show that owners earn more from rooms they never fill. I would not state that as fact.
- What the sources do support is that fixed costs run whether or not a room sells. They also show how big OTA commission and GST are on each sale.
- A safer payoff line: "an empty room costs you rent, salary and EMI. A sold room pays only after the platform and tax take their share."

**1. Cost to build or convert (per key and for 20 rooms)**
- Budget/economy new-build is about ₹53.2 lakh per key, excluding land, in the 2025 Savills-Hotelivate benchmark. [https://brandsync.co.in/hotel-construction-cost-india.html] This is a secondary summary of the benchmark. The same source gives ₹3.3 crore per key for luxury.
- The older Hotelivate 2023 survey (481 hotels) put budget/economy at ₹36.62 lakh per key. [https://hotelivate.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Hotel-Development-Cost-Survey-2023.pdf] The 2021 survey had the same figure, ₹36.61 lakh, and that one included land. [https://hotelivate.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/2021-Hotel-Development-Cost-Survey-India.pdf]
- These surveys cover branded hotels of all sizes, so a 20-room independent can cost much less.
- A 20-room budget hotel, new-build in a Tier-II city, may need ₹3–5 crore including land, building, interiors, FF&E and working capital. [https://projectreportbank.com/small-hotel-project-report-bank-loan/] This is a CA's illustrative range, not survey data.
- Conversion of an existing building costs about ₹5–6 lakh per key for a full room renovation. [https://brandsync.co.in/hotel-construction-cost-india.html]
- Illustrative ₹4.00 crore project for 20 rooms (Tier-II budget hotel). [https://projectreportbank.com/bank-loan-small-hotel-project-finance/]
  - Renovation and interiors ₹2.20 crore.
  - FF&E ₹0.70 crore.
  - Equipment ₹0.40 crore.
  - Pre-opening and contingency ₹0.35 crore.
  - Working-capital margin ₹0.35 crore.
  - Promoter puts in ₹1.40 crore and the term loan is ₹2.60 crore.
- FF&E for 20 rooms is ₹65,000–₹1,10,000 per room plus ₹12–22 lakh for common areas, ₹25–44 lakh in total. [https://projectreportbank.com/small-hotel-equipment-furniture-ffe-cost/]
- Gap: I found no reliable public lease rent per key. The only rent figure is the monthly range in section 5.

**2. Occupancy, ADR and RevPAR benchmarks (2025)**
- India overall: 64% occupancy, ₹8,624 ADR, ₹5,522 RevPAR. [https://mmrhotels.com/resources/indian-hospitality-industry/] This is Horwath HTL / CoStar data.
- Midscale and economy tier: 56.7% occupancy, ₹4,049 ADR, ₹2,294 RevPAR. [https://mmrhotels.com/resources/indian-hospitality-industry/]
- Excluding aggregator-listed hotels, that tier is 64.1%, ₹4,666 and ₹2,988. [https://mmrhotels.com/resources/indian-hospitality-industry/]
- Insider fact: the average budget-tier room earns ₹2,294 a night even though its average rate is ₹4,049. RevPAR is the room rate spread across the empty rooms.
- Treebo's own claim is 75%+ occupancy against an industry average of 50–55%. [https://forefind.com/franchises/treebo-hotels/] This is old marketing copy from a third-party listing and is unverified.
- Regional spread for branded hotels in 2025-26: South India 70.8% occupancy, North India 64.5%. [https://www.asianhospitality.com/indias-hotel-pipeline-nears-existing-supply/]
- East India is the lowest-performing region. [https://www.asianhospitality.com/indias-hotel-pipeline-nears-existing-supply/]

**3. OTA commission (MakeMyTrip, Booking.com)**
- Hotels pay OTAs 15–25% of the room rate. MakeMyTrip/Goibibo charge 15–25%, with most independents paying 18–22%. Booking.com charges 15–18%. [https://www.onlinehotelier.com/guides/ota/what-is-ota.html]
- Other sources put Booking.com at 15–20% and MakeMyTrip at 18–25%. [https://apycue.com/blog/the-real-cost-of-ota-commissions-a-hotel-owners-guide]
- One source says standalone hotels pay 22–40% on MakeMyTrip, against 15–25% for chains. [https://frontdesko.app/ota-commission-cost-data-independent-hotels] It is a secondary source, so treat it as unverified.
- Example from a source: a ₹4,000 room at 20% commission means the OTA keeps ₹800. [https://apycue.com/blog/the-real-cost-of-ota-commissions-a-hotel-owners-guide]
- 18% GST is charged on top of the commission itself. [https://www.exceedhms.com/ota-commission-calculator.php]
- The real rate is often higher than the contract. Visibility boosters and promotions push many hotels' blended cost closer to 22% than the 15% they remember signing. [https://www.exceedhms.com/ota-commission-calculator.php]
- Booking.com's Preferred Partner programme adds 3–5% to commission. [https://blog.jhattse.com/hotel-ota-commission-rates-india-2026/]
- If 60–70% of bookings come via OTAs at 15–20%, the hotel loses 9–14% of total room revenue to commissions. [https://www.onlinehotelier.com/tools/revenue-profit-estimator/]
- Rate parity: you cannot undercut the OTA price on your own website. [https://apycue.com/blog/the-real-cost-of-ota-commissions-a-hotel-owners-guide]
- The Go-MMT group holds about 50% of India's domestic online hotel booking market. [https://www.onlinehotelier.com/guides/ota/what-is-ota.html]
- The Competition Commission of India (CCI) pulled up MakeMyTrip and OYO. FHRAI, Treebo and FabHotels complained about collusion and abuse of dominance. [https://finshots.in/archive/makemytrip-and-oyo-are-partners-in-crime/]

**4. GST on room tariff (the ₹3,000 room)**
- From 22 Sept 2025, rooms up to ₹7,500 a night attract 5% GST with no input tax credit (ITC). Rooms above ₹7,500 attract 18% with ITC. [https://www.hotelogix.com/blog/gst-rate-on-hotel-rooms]
- Before that, the lower slab was 12% with ITC. [https://blog.petpooja.com/finance-compliance/gst-on-hotel-rooms-sl
